correctness.rationale: The directed-union proof reduces every finite-dimensional smash-product test space to one directed stage because only finitely many module vectors occur in its polynomial coefficients. The same Følner subspace then works after inclusion. Finite direct sums follow from the published exact-sequence two-of-three theorem, arbitrary direct sums from directed unions, and the maximal-submodule/radical conclusions follow from quotient and extension closure. Quantifiers and scope are explicit; no computation substitutes for a proof.

value.rationale: The result upgrades a newly introduced permanence theorem into categorical structure: a localizing Serre class and a canonical functorial maximal extensively amenable submodule for every module. This is useful precisely because it gives a decomposition tool in settings where the source motivates extensive amenability as better behaved than ordinary module amenability. The claim is structural rather than a renaming or finite parameter increment.
